A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSD/Saguaro research, with matching authors and complete appendices A-F. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, experiments, and displays.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding-throughput, cache-hit, sampling, and fallback experiments for Llama-3 and Qwen-3 in Sections 4-5 and Appendices B and F.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical studies and adds baseline parameter-sweep results in Appendix B.4, Tables 1-2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Saguaro's cache construction, sampling scheme, and batch-dependent fallback procedure remain unchanged, including their descriptions in the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HumanEval, Alpaca, GSM8k, and UltraFeedback with the same Llama-3 and Qwen-3 model families. The added baseline sweeps vary configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The autoregressive, ordinary SD, SGLang/vLLM standalone SD, and EAGLE-3 comparators are already described in v1. v3 tunes these existing methods without changing comparator membership in the corresponding main figures. DSI and Mirror-SD are related-work additions only.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 adds SGLang sweeps over steps 2-14 and topk 1-5, and vLLM sweeps over lookahead K=2,4,6,8,10,12. Dataset counts, generation lengths, hardware, and throughput metric remain unchanged. B.2 still describes five draft tokens, leaving the connection between sweep selections and updated figures incompletely documented.

E4.justification: New baseline sensitivity analyses show how lookahead and tree configuration affect throughput and identify the best feasible configurations. Existing Saguaro analyses of fan-out, temperature, sampling downweighting, and fallback strategy are retained.

E5.justification: There are no changes to repeated-run or seed disclosures, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance testing. The new baseline tables report point throughputs without additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 1, 6, and 7 revise Llama results, and Tables 1-2 add tuning outcomes. Figure 1 changes the vLLM/SGLang SD ratios from 1.7x/2.6x to 2.1x/3.1x; Figure 7 changes average SSD/AR from 4.7x to 4.8x. New SGLang maxima are 201.9 tok/s for standalone SD and 192.8 for EAGLE-3. These are revised comparisons alongside added tuning, not established same-setting gains. Appendix B.3 and Qwen results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, speedup bounds, cache-topology derivations, sampling results, fallback theorem, and all Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, evaluation summary, and conclusion replace 'up to 2x' over optimized speculative decoding with 'on average 30% faster' than the strongest baselines. This changes the quantitative claim and its aggregation; the lossless parallelization contribution, autoregressive speedup claim, and Pareto-frontier claim remain.

C2.justification: Appendix B.4 newly explains missing configurations as consequences of library bugs and restricts the vLLM sweep because tree-verification codepaths are incomplete. Existing mechanism explanations, compute tradeoffs, and SSD limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 documents parameter grids, best configurations, and compatibility restrictions. Conversely, Section 4.3.3 removes the explicit F=1 and one-draft-H100 statement for Figure 6 without specifying a replacement. Core implementation details, software versions, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds DSI (Timor et al., 2025) and Mirror-SD (Bhendawade et al., 2025), explaining their overlapping drafting/verification approaches. It also shortens the SpecBranch comparison by dropping its dynamic hyperparameter-selection description. The broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the headline performance wording, related-work paragraph, acknowledgements, and new Appendix B.4 subsection. Most prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 1-2, revises titles and axis labels in Figures 1, 6, and 7, and changes spacing and appendix figure placement. Figures 9-12 are redistributed across pages rather than newly introduced; most existing displays remain intact.

improvement.justification: The baseline sweeps make comparator tuning more assessable, support the revised average-advantage claim, and disclose implementation restrictions; added related work improves attribution. The benefit is limited by inconsistent updates: B.2 retains five-token settings, B.3 retains 4.68x average SSD/AR while Figure 7 shows 4.8x, and Figure 6 loses its fan-out disclosure. These issues temper an overall improvement in empirical transparency.
